concerns.text: Only **5 independent runs per variant** are planned (total 30 runs). This sample size is far too small to achieve adequate statistical power for detecting the claimed ≥60 % CPU‑time reduction and ≥80 % performance‑retention, even with bootstrapping. The plan acknowledges low power (< 0.8) but still expects to meet significance thresholds, which is unsound.

The fallback to a Kaggle T4 GPU if the model cannot load on CPU introduces a hardware confound. Runs that switch to GPU will have different CPU‑time characteristics, violating the assumption that per‑step CPU cost is comparable across variants.

concerns.location: plan.md:Training Protocol (line ~55) and Compute Feasibility Strategy (line ~120)
concerns.text: Early‑stopping when average reward ≥ 0.8 may cause the Student‑Only variant to terminate earlier than the Baseline. Comparing **per‑step** CPU time under such differing episode counts can conflate convergence speed with computational efficiency, biasing the SC‑002 cost‑reduction claim.

RQ1 and RQ2 are framed as causal statements (e.g., “Student‑Only gating can replace the teacher‑student confidence gap”). The experimental design is purely comparative/observational and does not control for all pathways that could affect performance, so causal inference is not justified.
